title: From Malthusian stagnation to sustained growth
summary: Population and technology fed each other for millennia; once technological change rewarded education, families traded quantity of children for quality and growth took off.

title: Out of Africa: diversity and development
summary: Diversity falls with migratory distance from East Africa; it spurs innovation but erodes cohesion, so intermediate levels are best for development.

title: Geography, agriculture and culture as deep roots of prosperity
summary: Biogeography set the timing of farming and the crops grown; these shaped states, future orientation and gender norms, and institutions and culture carry the effects forward.

title: The Church dissolved intensive kinship, producing WEIRD psychology
summary: The Western Church's marriage and family programme broke up clans and cousin marriage; weaker kinship made people more individualistic, analytic, impartial and trusting of strangers.

title: Weak kinship opened the way to towns, law and representative government
summary: Freed from clans, Europeans formed voluntary associations — charter towns, guilds, universities — whose competition produced impersonal law and representative government.

title: Markets and benign competition built impersonal prosociality
summary: Market integration and competition between groups raise trust and fairness toward strangers, patience and work effort, which in turn feed prosperity.

title: Moralizing gods and ritual scaled up cooperation
summary: Rituals bind groups, and beliefs in punishing, all-seeing gods extend fairness to strangers, letting societies grow larger.

title: Monogamous marriage tamed male competition
summary: Polygyny creates pools of unmarried men and higher testosterone; imposed monogamy lowers crime and inequality and raises trust and self-control.

title: Bigger, better-connected collective brains drove innovation
summary: Cities, associations, literacy and individualism widened the flow of ideas, so innovation accelerated long before industrialization.

title: Rice and irrigation sustain clans and holistic thinking
summary: Paddy rice and irrigation reward clan-based cooperation, which goes with less analytic and less individualistic psychology.

title: Synthesis: Protestant literacy as the bridge from culture to the demographic transition
summary: Henrich's Protestant literacy meets Galor's human-capital engine: scriptural literacy raises human capital, which lowers fertility and lifts growth.
